title: Localizing the Sycophancy Override: Where User Pressure Suppresses Truthful Recall

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: if the sycophancy override mechanism is localizable, it becomes a concrete target for fine-tuning or inference-time intervention. This directly bridges interpretability findings to deployment-level safety improvements.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires familiarity with TransformerLens, activation patching, residual stream analysis, and ablation studies. These are specialized mechanistic interpretability techniques beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: construct paired prompts, apply activation patching to identify override location, ablate/clamp and measure effect. Well-defined experimental pipeline with clear output.

novelty.reasoning: Directly relevant work exists: 'When Truth Is Overridden: Uncovering the Internal Origins of Sycophancy in Large Language Models' (arXiv:2508.02087, 2025) investigates the information flow dynamics causing sycophantic behavior and addresses the internal origins of the sycophancy override. Activation patching is standard methodology (reviewed in arXiv:2407.02646, Oct 2025). 'Adversarial Activation Patching' (arXiv:2507.09406, 2025) applies the framework to deception detection. However, the specific goal of localizing the exact (layer, head) where user pressure overrides truthful recall, and then clamping/ablating to restore truthfulness, may still have unexplored aspects beyond what the existing paper covers.
